def-image.title: Image
def-image.html:
Let f:V→W be a linear transformation. Define the image of f by im(f):={w∈W:w=f(v) for some v∈V}.

i.e. The image contains all the possible outputs of the function f.

def-kernel.title: Kernel
def-kernel.html:
Let f:V→W be a linear transformation. Define the kernel of f by ker(f):={v∈V:f(v)=0W}.

i.e. The kernel contains everything in the domain that becomes the zero vector under f.

def-linear-transformation.title: Linear Transformation
def-linear-transformation.html:
Let V,W be vector spaces over F. A function T:V→W is called a linear transformation (or linear map), if

  1. T(v1+v2)=T(v1)+T(v2), for all v1,v2∈V;
  2. T(λv)=λT(v), for all λ∈F and v∈V.

def-nullity.title: Nullity
def-nullity.html: Let f:V→W be a linear transformation. The nullity of f is defined by nullity(f):=dim⁡(ker(f)).

def-rank.title: Rank
def-rank.html: Let f:V→W be a linear transformation. The rank of f is defined by rank(f):=dim⁡(im(f)).

exm-complex-conjugation.title: Complex Conjugation
exm-complex-conjugation.html: Determine whether complex conjugation T:C→C defined by T(z)=z―, where a+bi―=a−bi, is a linear transformation.

exm-constant-function.title: Constant Function
exm-constant-function.html: Determine whether T:R→R defined by T(x)=5 for all x∈R is a linear transformation.

exm-coordinate-transformation.title: A Specific Matrix Transformation
exm-coordinate-transformation.html: Determine whether T:F3→F2 defined by T(a1,a2,a3)=(2a1+a3,a2−a1) is a linear transformation.

exm-deter.html: Is it possible to have a linear map f:R2→R3 such that f(1,0)=(2,3,4),f(1,1)=(3,4,5),f(2,3)=(4,56)?

exm-deter-two.html: Suppose we are give a linear transformation f:R[x]≤3→R[x]≤2. And it is also know that f(x3)=3x2,f(x2)=2x,f(x)=1,f(1)=0.

exm-differentiation.title: Differentiation
exm-differentiation.html: Determine whether D:R[x]→R[x] defined by D(f(x))=f′(x) (the derivative) is a linear transformation.

exm-differentiation-kernel-image.title: Differentiation
exm-differentiation-kernel-image.html: Let D:R[x]≤3→R[x]≤2 be defined by D(f(x))=f′(x). Find the kernel and image of D.

exm-identity.title: Identity Map
exm-identity.html: Let V be a vector space. Determine whether the identity map idV:V→V defined by idV(v)=v is a linear transformation.

exm-inclusion.title: Inclusion Map
exm-inclusion.html: Let W⊆V be a subspace. Determine whether the inclusion map ι:W↪V defined by ι(w)=w is a linear transformation.

exm-integration.title: Integration
exm-integration.html: Determine whether T:R[x]→R[x] defined by T(f(x))=∫0xf(t)dt is a linear transformation.

exm-matrix-composition.title: Composition Operator
exm-matrix-composition.html: Fix a continuous function g:R→R. Determine whether the composition operator Cg:C(R)→C(R) defined by Cg(f)=f∘g, i.e., Cg(f)(x)=f(g(x)), is a linear transformation.

exm-matrix-transformation.title: Left Multiplication by a Matrix
exm-matrix-transformation.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) be an m×n matrix. Determine whether fA:Fn→Fm defined by fA(v)=Av (where v is viewed as a column vector) is a linear transformation.

exm-multiplication-by-x.title: Multiplication by x
exm-multiplication-by-x.title_html: Multiplication by x
exm-multiplication-by-x.html: Determine whether T:F[x]→F[x] defined by T(f(x))=x⋅f(x) is a linear transformation.

exm-norm.title: Norm
exm-norm.html: Determine whether T:Rn→R defined by T(v)=∥v∥ (the Euclidean norm) is a linear transformation.

exm-nullity-rank-diff.html: Recall that for D:R[x]≤3→R[x]≤2 defined by D(f(x))=f′(x), we have ker(D)=R and im(D)=R[x]≤2. Compute the nullity and rank of D.

exm-projection.title: Projection onto a Coordinate Axis
exm-projection.html: Determine whether T:R2→R2 defined by T(a1,a2)=(a1,0) is a linear transformation.

exm-rotation.title: Rotation in the Plane
exm-rotation.html: Determine whether rotation by angle θ (counterclockwise) in the plane is a linear transformation. That is, let Tθ:R2→R2 be the rotation map.

exm-shift.title: Shift Operator
exm-shift.html: Fix θ∈R. Determine whether the shift operator Sθ:C(R)→C(R) defined by Sθ(f)(x)=f(x−θ) is a linear transformation. (This operator translates the graph of f by θ units to the right.)

exm-squaring.title: Squaring
exm-squaring.html: Determine whether T:F2→F2 defined by T(a1,a2)=(a12,0) is a linear transformation.

exm-trace-kernel-image.title: Trace
exm-trace-kernel-image.html: Let tr:M2(R)→R be defined by tr(A)=a11+a22. Find the kernel and image of tr.

exm-trace-matrices.title: Trace
exm-trace-matrices.html: Determine whether the trace function tr:Mn(F)→F defined by tr(A)=∑i=1naii is a linear transformation.

exm-translation.title: Translation
exm-translation.html: Determine whether T:R2→R2 defined by T(v)=v+c for some fixed nonzero c∈R2 is a linear transformation.

exm-zero-map.title: Zero Map
exm-zero-map.html: For any vector spaces V and W, determine whether the zero map 0:V→W defined by 0(v)=0W for all v∈V is a linear transformation.

thm-equivalent-condition.title: Equivalent Characterization of Linearity
thm-equivalent-condition.html: Let V,W be vector spaces over F and T:V→W be a function. Then T is a linear transformation if and only if T(αv1+βv2)=αT(v1)+βT(v2) for all α,β∈F and v1,v2∈V.

thm-linear-combination.title: Linear Maps Preserve Linear Combinations
thm-linear-combination.html: Let T:V→W be a linear transformation. Then for any vectors v1,…,vn∈V and scalars a1,…,an∈F: T(∑i=1naivi)=∑i=1naiT(vi).

thm-linear-transform-basis.title: Linear Transformations are Determined by Their Action on a Basis
thm-linear-transform-basis.title_html: Linear Transformations are Determined by Their Action on a Basis
thm-linear-transform-basis.html:
Let T:V→W be a linear transformation and V is finite dimensional, and B={v1,…,vn} be a basis for V. Then we have:

  1. For every v∈V, f(v) is a linear combination of f(v1),f(v2),…,f(vn).
  2. Suppose the linear transformation g:V→W satisfies g(vi)=f(vi) for all i. Then g=f.

We say ‘f is determined by f(v1),…,f(vn)’ in this case.

thm-preserves-negation.title: Linear Maps Preserve Negation
thm-preserves-negation.html: Let T:V→W be a linear transformation. Then T(−v)=−T(v) for all v∈V.

thm-prop-image.title: Properties of Image
thm-prop-image.html:
Let f:V→W be a linear transformation. Then:

  1. im(f) is a subspace of W;

  2. f is surjective iff im(f)=W.

thm-prop-kernel.title: Properties of Kernel
thm-prop-kernel.html:
Let f:V→W be a linear transformation. Then:

  1. ker(f) is a subspace of V;

  2. f is injective iff ker(f)={0V}.

thm-rank-nullity.title: Rank-Nullity Theorem
thm-rank-nullity.html: Let V be a finite dimensional vector space and f:V→W be a linear transformation. Then we have nullity(f)+rank(f)=dim⁡(V).

thm-zero-maps-to-zero.title: Zero Maps to Zero
thm-zero-maps-to-zero.html: Let T:V→W be a linear transformation. Then T(0V)=0W.
